policy: Primary or authoritative sources support the factual bridge; workplace practices remain explicitly labelled LAiDIES interpretations.

profiles.support: Lovelace's Oxford-hosted primary Notes contain the Bernoulli-number working table and ordered operations; Oxford's History of Science Museum describes the diagram as a stepwise program.

Computer History Museum documents Hopper's Mark I work, compiler development and COBOL contribution and explains higher-level language translation. The public AI-interface analogy was narrowed to mediation rather than faithful compiler-style translation.

The 1942 patent names Lamarr and Antheil and describes synchronized frequency changes intended to make signals harder to discover, decipher or block; the National Inventors Hall of Fame documents the later spread-spectrum lineage.

Spärck Jones's paper defines collection-frequency term specificity and greater weight for rare terms; Cambridge preserves her IR/NLP record; the original RAG paper supplies the retrieval-before-generation bridge. The public copy now distinguishes missing retrieved support from an answer generated from model parameters.

Cambridge confirms Fry's public-understanding chair and engagement with people affected by technical systems; OECD and NIST support the AI-literacy, human-agency and sociotechnical bridge. The public copy removed an unmeasured adoption-speed comparison.

Stanford confirms Li's roles and ImageNet contribution; the original ImageNet paper documents its ontology and human voting; the fairness paper addresses representation choices. The public copy now distinguishes human choices in all datasets from human-applied labels in supervised datasets.
DAIR documents Gebru's role and research philosophy; the author-hosted Stochastic Parrots paper covers scale costs, data opacity, documentation, stakeholder values and the risks of fluent output.
Thomas's official profile documents her fast.ai, CADE and QUT roles; her published work frames data ethics as practical technical work and argues for affected people as design partners with recourse.

MIT Media Lab and the Gender Shades project document intersectional evaluation of commercial gender classifiers and large subgroup accuracy disparities, supporting disaggregated evaluation rather than one overall score.

Crawford's official profile confirms current roles; Yale's Atlas of AI description documents minerals, labour, data, power and planetary costs; the IEA documents AI and data-centre energy consequences.

AI Now and Signal document Whittaker's roles and privacy-infrastructure work; NIST and FTC document data minimization, surveillance incentives, profiling and inference. The public definition was narrowed to acknowledge proxy inference.

Bender's University of Washington profile confirms her roles; primary ACL and Stochastic Parrots papers distinguish linguistic form from meaning and document the risk of reading fluent pattern continuation as grounded understanding.

IEEE documents the six programmers and their procedural techniques; Smithsonian preserves the archival record; the ILO documents less-visible human labelling and review work behind modern AI. The public copy now says this labour affects many systems rather than every system.
MIT identifies Hamilton as leader of the team that developed Apollo guidance software; NASA documents the Apollo 11 priority, overload and restart behaviour used as the system-level teaching bridge.

IBM and ACM document Allen's compiler optimisation and automatic parallelisation work; the IEA documents current AI compute and energy consequences. The unsupported batching reference was removed from the public copy.

UW-Madison identifies Wahba's smoothing-spline work as foundational to data science and machine learning; her own materials connect smoothing splines, penalized fitting, regularization and generalization error.

Harvard identifies Dwork as a co-inventor of differential privacy and describes it as a rigorous privacy guarantee; Harvard materials explain the participation guarantee and composition risk across analyses.
insitro identifies Koller as founder and CEO; her Stanford research page documents probabilistic models and machine learning in domains with substantial uncertainty.
MIT materials describe abstraction through interfaces and specifications, independent modules, and substituting an implementation that satisfies the same specification.
The Computer History Museum documents Sammet's programming-language work, COBOL committee service, FORMAC leadership and programming-language history.

Computer History Museum records Goldberg's Xerox PARC and Smalltalk work and its relationship to object-oriented programming and graphical interface concepts; the Smalltalk-72 manual supplies contemporary technical context.

MIT documents Goldwasser and Micali's introduction of probabilistic encryption and Goldwasser, Micali and Rackoff's introduction of zero-knowledge proofs; MIT also confirms her current appointments and cryptography work.

Conway's University of Michigan archive documents the Mead-Conway VLSI methodology, intentionally simplified design rules, teaching materials and implementation infrastructure that widened participation.
Thinking Machines Lab identifies Murati as co-founder and CEO and describes its work in collaborative, customizable AI that people can understand and adapt.
Anthropic identifies Amodei as co-founder and President with leadership spanning research, engineering, product, governance, commercial execution and the executive team.

Google DeepMind identifies Ibrahim as COO and Responsibility and Safety Council co-chair and says the council evaluates research, projects and collaborations against AI Principles with research and product teams. The public contribution was narrowed to that documented structure.

OpenAI identifies Simo as CEO of Applications and describes Applications as the business and operational functions responsible for how research reaches and benefits the world; the workflow test is labelled LAiDIES interpretation.

Stanford documents Finn's appointments, Physical Intelligence co-founding and robotic-interaction research; Physical Intelligence materials document multi-stage robotic tasks. The public profile was narrowed to the feedback-loop discipline supported by this work.

Anthropic's constitution identifies Askell as leading Character work and primary author of Claude's Constitution and describes the constitution's role in shaping values, behaviour and training trade-offs.
Miller's official current site documents her AI business leadership, advising, investing and prior AWS machine-learning role; the measurement and workflow method is labelled LAiDIES interpretation.
